name: Real Estate

automations.title: Buyer Pipeline Nurture & Showing Follow-Up System
automations.summary: When a buyer attends a showing, the agent receives an automatic post-showing survey to capture the buyer's reaction, and the buyer gets a follow-up…
steps: When a buyer attends a showing, the agent receives an automatic post-showing survey to capture the buyer's reaction, and the buyer gets a follow-up text within an hour with similar active listings based on their stated criteria.

Buyers who go 10 days without an active showing are flagged for a check-in call prompt, and buyers who have toured more than five homes are automatically moved into a "decision stage" nurture sequence with market urgency messaging, keeping the pipeline moving without the agent manually tracking where every buyer stands across a dozen open conversations.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a real estate agent / broker handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: CRM (e.g., Follow Up Boss or LionDesk)

automations.title: Lease Renewal Campaign & Vacancy Launch System
automations.summary: Ninety days before each lease expiration, tenants automatically receive a personalized renewal offer with the new rate and a deadline to respond.
steps: Ninety days before each lease expiration, tenants automatically receive a personalized renewal offer with the new rate and a deadline to respond.
Tenants who don't respond by the 60-day mark get a follow-up text from the property manager.
Those who decline trigger the marketing workflow automatically, photos ordered, listing drafted, and the unit posted to Zillow and Apartments.com, all before the current tenant has even moved out.
The property manager never scrambles to fill a vacancy that was announced two weeks before move-out.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a property manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Property management platform (e.g., Buildium, AppFolio, or Propertyware)

automations.title: Instant Lead Response & Booking System
automations.summary: When a new inquiry lands from Zillow, Realtor.com, or the brokerage's own website, the system fires an automatic text and email within 60 seconds…
steps: When a new inquiry lands from Zillow, Realtor.com, or the brokerage's own website, the system fires an automatic text and email within 60 seconds, introducing the assigned agent, attaching the listing details, and dropping in a direct link to book a showing on the agent's calendar.
Leads who don't respond within 15 minutes get a second, shorter nudge, and any lead who books a showing is instantly added to the CRM with a tag noting the source campaign.

Most buyer inquiries go cold within the first half hour, so cutting response time from the industry-average 30-plus minutes down to under a minute keeps far more leads in an active conversation instead of calling the next agent on the list.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, an internet lead coordinator has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Self-Scheduled Showing Booking System

steps: Instead of buyers and agents trading four or five texts to find a time that works, this system publishes each agent's live availability to a public booking page linked from every listing and marketing email.

Buyers pick an open slot, the request is checked against the seller's showing instructions (lockbox code, pet warning, showing window), and a confirmation with driving directions goes out immediately by text and email.
The agent's calendar updates in real time across every device, and a reminder fires two hours before the appointment to cut down on no-shows.
What used to take a dozen back-and-forth messages per showing now takes under 90 seconds of the buyer's time.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a showing coordinator spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

Serious buyers in competitive markets can lose a home to a same-day offer, so shrinking the alert delay from the typical 24-hour MLS sync down to under 10 minutes has turned "I saw it on Zillow first" into a rare complaint instead of a routine one.

Buyers who click through to a partner link are logged in the CRM, letting the brokerage track which service referrals actually get used and strengthening those partnerships over time.
What used to be a nice-to-have an agent occasionally remembered to send now reaches every closed buyer automatically, adding real value at the exact moment it matters most.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a move concierge re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

steps: When a listing's term expires without a sale, the automation automatically detects the status change and triggers an outreach sequence to the seller within 24 hours, opening with a low-pressure email offering a free updated market re-evaluation rather than a hard sales pitch.

Sellers who click into the market re-evaluation link are automatically flagged as warm and moved to the top of the outreach queue.
Instead of a seller feeling abandoned the moment their listing quietly expires, they hear from the brokerage the same day with a real plan for next steps.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a listing renewal specialist, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Load-Balanced Team Lead Distribution System
automations.summary: Instead of routing new leads through a fixed round-robin, this automation continuously tracks each team agent's current open lead count and recent…
steps: Instead of routing new leads through a fixed round-robin, this automation continuously tracks each team agent's current open lead count and recent average response time, then assigns every incoming lead to whichever agent can actually respond the fastest right now.

An agent who's slammed with showings and has been slow to respond over the last few days automatically receives fewer new leads until their response time recovers, while a fast-responding agent with bandwidth gets a heavier share.
The team lead dispatcher gets a weekly summary showing distribution and response metrics per agent, making coaching conversations data-driven instead of anecdotal.
Leads that used to sit with an overloaded agent for hours now land with someone who can call back in minutes, meaningfully lifting the team's overall conversion rate.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a team lead dispatcher has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

Each platform receives a properly formatted version: a short vertical clip for Instagram and TikTok, a full walkthrough for YouTube and the MLS listing itself, and a preview embed for the email blast.
Listings with a virtual tour attached within the first hour of going live see meaningfully higher early engagement than those where the tour trickles out over a day or two.
What used to take up to a full afternoon of manual uploading now finishes in minutes.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a multimedia marketing coordinator has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

The investor relations manager no longer has to manually cross-reference a spreadsheet of buy-boxes against the daily hot sheet; the matching happens continuously in the background across every active investor at once.
Investors who reply expressing interest are automatically flagged in the CRM for same-day follow-up.

automations.manualProcess: Without this system, an investor relations manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

steps: As soon as a property under an HOA goes under contract, the automation automatically identifies the governing association from the property record and sends a document request to the HOA management company for the resale certificate, governing documents, financial statements, and any pending litigation disclosures required for closing.

Once documents arrive, they're automatically uploaded to the transaction file and the buyer's agent is notified.
A step that used to get forgotten until someone asked whether the HOA docs had arrived a week before closing now starts itself the same day the contract is signed.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a hoa liaison, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

steps: When a deal's status changes to closed in the transaction platform, the automation automatically pulls the final sale price and the agent's commission agreement on file, calculates the exact split between agent, broker, and any referral fees owed, and generates a disbursement request that routes directly to the accounting manager for approval.

Approved disbursements are logged automatically for monthly reconciliation and year-end reporting.
Agents get paid faster, and the accounting manager spends far less time chasing down closed-deal paperwork.
